chapter: Music as a way of life
title: Rehearsals, fruit business and his music collection
summary: He recalls rehearsing in 1922, says he now peddles fruit, and shows a trunk of sheet music he kept.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And have three or four watermelons. Three or four watermelons. Pot of red, beat the rice. He used to wake in a watermelon. The fruit business. That's what I do now.
I'm still in the fruit business. I peddle, you see. Yeah. Yeah, I have my truck out there. Big, minor red beans, rice.

Always did have a large house. Just me and my wife, all my kids is gone. Plenty of company on, plenty of room. I got a whole trunk of music out there. We bought more music and then the two bands sit on there. Harry and I, these brothers, the old days, I love, we bought some music. Just buy music. Everything late come out, he'd come with a stack. Leo, he'd come with a stack. I'd get down and sometimes he'd have three, four copies of the same number.
We used to join these different music clubs, you see. Yeah. And every number come out. Sometimes three music clubs will send you the same number, you know what I mean? As they come out to me.
I got a whole trunk of Raymond out there from Louis Armstrong, bought some Walter Pesaw made. I just like music. I keep all that stuff so straight. That's good to keep it. You never tell.
